coaching.title: Today's Run
coaching.message: You're 52 days out and in taper—but your recovery score of 7/100 and resting HR of 86 (vs. your 30-day avg of 63.4) tells me you're still heavily fatigued. This is a Tuesday, which would normally be quality work, but your body is screaming no. Run 6–8 easy miles at Z2 (roughly 135–145 bpm based on your recent data) with no intensity. The Julian Alps 50K demands mountain-specific durability, not more glycogen depletion right now. Taper works only if you actually recover into it.

coaching.title: Fuel Right
coaching.message: Your 5.53h sleep at 48% efficiency means you're running a metabolic deficit and parasympathetic debt. Eat 1.2g carbs per kg bodyweight today—prioritize it around your run and in the 90 minutes after. Aim for 25–30g protein at each meal to stabilize cortisol. Given the sparse aid at Julian Alps, your gut needs to be bulletproof on real food, not gels. Use today's easy run as a dress rehearsal: test whatever you'll race with (solid carbs, electrolytes, hydration volume).

coaching.title: Recovery
coaching.message: Sleep is your limiting factor—48% efficiency on 5.53 hours is the red flag here. Tonight: no screens after 21:00, cool room (65–68°F), consider 200mg magnesium glycinate 90 minutes before bed. You're likely traveling for work; prioritize a familiar pillow and blackout curtains over anything else. By race week, you need 8+ hours. Use this taper window to front-load sleep debt now, not sprint into Kranjska Gora depleted.

coaching.title: Mental Edge
coaching.message: You're deep in taper and the niggle of restlessness is real—but easy runs and early sleep aren't retreat, they're precision. Julian Alps demands tactical pacing through sparse aid and steep vert; that's won on legs that recovered, not on volume squeezed in now. Trust the plan. In 52 days you'll need every percent of autonomic nervous system balance you can muster. Patience is the weapon.
